'''Uonuma Shrine''' (魚沼神社, ''Uonuma Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Ojiya, Niigata|Ojiya]], [[Niigata Prefecture]]. The shrine grounds include the nationally designated Important Cultural Property, the Amida Hall.

== Enshrined deities ==
* [[Ame-no-Kaguyama]]
* [[Toyotama-hime-no-Mikoto]] 
* Ahi-no-kami (Ahiko)

== History ==
The shrine's foundation is traditionally attributed to the reign of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|qid=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}. The name "Uonuma Shrine" appears in documents from the [[Heian period]] and is recorded in the ''[[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]'' among the five shrines in [[Uonuma District]]. However, its identification as the same Uonuma Shrine listed in the ''Engishiki'' has been debated since the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}. 

During the [[Sengoku period (Japan)|Sengoku period]], due to its shared deity with [[Yahiko Shrine]] in [[Yahiko, Niigata|Yahiko]], it was referred to as "Kami-Yahiko Shrine." Historical documents from the era of [[Uesugi Kenshin]] mention it as "Kami-Yahiko Daimyōjin," and a plaque reading "Yahiko Daimyōjin" is displayed in the worship hall. The shrine served as a religious center for the region and was later called "Uonuma Shrine" during the {{ill|Bakumatsu|en|Bakumatsu|qid=Q804558|lt=Bakumatsu}} period. It was relocated to its current location in Tsuchikawa from the earlier site at Kaminoyama.

Key historical milestones include:
* [[Jōgan 3]] (861 CE): Uonuma Shrine received the Rank of [[Junior Fifth Rank|Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade]].
* [[Genkō 3]] (1333 CE): Shrine priests supported [[Nitta Yoshisada]] during his uprising.
* [[Eikyō 9]] (1437 CE): The shrine received a large gong donated by Saikata Yasaburō Mitsuyuki (now a Niigata Prefecture-designated cultural property).
* [[Eiroku 5]] (1562 CE): [[Uesugi Kenshin]] donated shrine lands and offerings for 18 branch shrines.
* [[Eiroku 12]] (1569 CE): A hand-copied version of the ''[[Daihannya-kyō]]'' was donated to the shrine.
* [[Meiji 6]] (1873 CE): Designated as a [[Gōsha]] and later promoted to [[Prefectural Shrine]].

== Shrine grounds ==
The main shrine gate is a [[Ryōbu torii]]. Adjacent to the purification fountain, stone steps lead to a historical water purification site. The shrine grounds include the Amida Hall to the left, the Kagura Hall to the right, and a monument commemorating the Russo-Japanese War nearby.

; Amida Hall
The Amida Hall, constructed in [[:en:1563 CE|1563 CE]] during the [[Muromachi period]], is designated as a National Important Cultural Property. It is a modest hōgyō-zukuri (hipped roof) structure with thatched roofing. Inside are statues of [[:en:Amida Nyorai|Amida Nyorai]] and [[:en:Dainichi Nyorai|Dainichi Nyorai]], said to have been crafted from iron sand sourced from the [[Shinano River]]. The hall was restored in [[:en:1954 CE|1954 CE]] to its original form.

== Cultural Properties ==
=== National Important Cultural Properties ===
* Amida Hall - Designated under the former Ancient Shrines and Temples Preservation Act in [[:en:1906 CE|1906 CE]].

=== Niigata Prefecture-Designated Cultural Properties ===
* Large Gong - Crafted in [[:en:1437 CE|1437 CE]] with inscriptions by Saikata Yasaburō Mitsuyuki.
* ''Daihannya-kyō'' (559 scrolls) - Donated in [[:en:1569 CE|1569 CE]].

=== Ojiya City-Designated Cultural Properties ===
* Mikoshi - A portable shrine featuring a phoenix on its roof, originally crafted in [[:en:1495 CE|1495 CE]] and restored in [[:en:1817 CE|1817 CE]].
* ''Uonuma Shrine Annual Event Record'' - Historical documents outlining shrine activities.

== Legends ==
=== Uesugi Kenshin and the Divine Army ===
Uesugi Kenshin is said to have visited the shrine to pray for victory before crossing the [[Shinano River]] en route to the [[Kantō region]]. During one such visit, he reportedly saw a vision of [[Ame-no-Kaguyama]] and other deities marching toward Kantō. The vision inspired his troops and contributed to their subsequent victories.

=== The Rescued Soldier ===
During [[World War II]], a soldier who had fallen into a dry well was rescued by a white-haired elderly man holding a lantern marked with "Kami-Yahiko Shrine." Upon being reunited with his unit, the elderly man disappeared.

=== The Giant Cedar ===
A massive cedar tree known as "Ōki-sama" stood on the shrine grounds until it was toppled by a storm. Its trunk reportedly stretched down the mountain, serving as a makeshift bridge.
